 Order

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company for reduction of the compensation awarded dated 18.08.2007 by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Dhar in Claim Case No.159/2006.
2.

The relevant facts of the case is that the respondent no.1 filed an application before the learned Tribunal alleging that the deceased Piyush Sanghvi was employed as conductor in the bus bearing registration no.MP-09- S-9500.
It is further alleged that on 26.06.2006 the driver of the bus drove the said bus rashly and negligently due to which, Piyush fell down and died.
Alleging to be dependent on the earnings of the deceased, they claimed compensation on various grounds.
3. Respondents no.5 and 6 proceeded ex-parte whereas the appellant contested the case denying the allegations and raised permissible defenses.

The learned Tribunal after holding an enquiry held that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving on the part of respondent no.5 and further taking income as Rs.4,500/- per month of the deceased, awarded compensation of Rs.6,62,500/-.
Being aggrieved by the same, the appellant filed this appeal.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the Tribunal grossly has erred in not considering the fact that the deceased himself was negligent as he was standing on the gate without taking any precautions, therefore, he himself ought to have been considered negligent for causing this accident and should have held to have contributed in causing this accident.

He further submitted that the Tribunal has erred in holding the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- without considering the nature of the work and without there being any cogent and positive evidence on record which is highly excessive and against the set principles.
Hence, the appellant prays for setting aside the impugned award passed against the appellant.
5. Learned counsel for the respondents/claimants supported the impugned award as regard the quantum and liability of compensation and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

6. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record of the Tribunal, the point is whether deceased himself was negligent as he was standing on the gate without taking any precautions.

On perusal of para 8 of the impugned award it is found that the witness Nikhil Jain stated that the gate of the bus was closed and did not state that gate was latched or not and Tribunal held that merely on this point, gate was latched or not deceased cannot be held liable for the contributory negligence.

It is also found that appellant had not pleaded this point in his pleadings,
therefore, the argument of the learned counsel for the appellant on this point without pleadings New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Ritu Sanghvi & 5 Ors. on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147602144/

sentences.text: cannot be sustained, the appellant had not dared to produce any evidence directly on this point.
Hence, there is no illegality in the finding of the Tribunal on this point.
The submission of the learned counsel for the appellant that deceased was also negligent has no substance.

7. Learned counsel for the appellant further contended that Tribunal has erred in relying the oral evidence and the salary certificate of the deceased and holding the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per month.

8. On this point, on perusing the record of the Tribunal, PW-4 Shiv Patel who is owner of the bus stated in examination that deceased was working as Conductor of the bus bearing registration no.MP-09-S-9500 and he issued the salary certificate Ex.P-8 stating that the salary of the deceased is Rs.4,500/- per month.
On perusal of the evidence of the owner of the offending bus, in the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal is correct in holding the income of the deceased as Rs.4,500/- per month.
9. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that there is no illegality in the impugned award passed by the Tribunal.
Hence, no case is made out for interference in the impugned award.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE RJ New India Assurance Co.Ltd. vs Smt.Ritu Sanghvi & 5 Ors. on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147602144/
